The edge-resize witness now awaits the committed Workspace projection before resolving final component geometry and percentage authority. A captured projection warning fails the witness. Both axes, active-tab persistence, Escape and reducer rejection keep their existing assertions.

Evidence: L3 (complete headed Chrome E2E with explicit Brain runtime) → L3 required. No residual acceptance criteria.

Change class: zero-delta — five added test lines; no production code or API change.

Micro-review eligible: existing projection-promise and captured-warning calls in one test.

| AC-1 | Both successful commits await `refreshPromise.then` after observing the changed document, before resolving the projected edge splitter. |

| AC-3 | All 41 original expect/poll expressions are token-identical; one warning assertion is added. |

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Placement is the whole review for a five-line diff, and it is right.**

The await lands after `const after = await readDocument()` — the commit is observed — and **before** `const settledConfig = (await findEdgeSplitter(edge))?.resizeConfig`. That ordering matters: `settledConfig` is captured post-projection, so the downstream `settledBand` read resolves `settledConfig.targetId` against a settled retained component rather than a stale one. Inserting after the config capture would have looked identical and fixed nothing.

**It closes a named failure I hold.** #17844's census records `WorkstationEdgeSplitterNL.spec.mjs` failing on *"left: the retained component adopts committed percentage authority"* — the exact assertion downstream of this insert, at `:315` in the PR head. One of the 29 unowned failures in that census, now attributed and repaired.

**Idiom note, carried from #18519 rather than repeated as a finding:** `callMethod(…, 'refreshPromise.then')` awaits one snapshot of a promise that is reassigned (`Workspace.mjs:1710/2393/2754`), where a generation-safe settle-probe counter already exists at `DockLockActionNL.spec.mjs:44`. Same mitigation applies — the barrier is followed by `expect.poll`, so an early return degrades to polling rather than a false pass, and a null throws loudly. With this PR the idiom is now used twice, which makes it the de facto pattern; if the two are ever unified, the counter is the stronger one. Not this PR's job.
